items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
items.summary: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

items.title: Team RIVER Volunteers
items.summary: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

items.venueAddress: West 174 Street and Amsterdam Avenue (in Highbridge Park)
items.summary: Summer Sports Experience Summer Sports Experience is an instructional youth program that teaches sports skills. Our knowledgeable NYC Parks staff train kids in sports such as basketball, ball hockey, kickball, flag football, pickleball, soccer, team handball, track and field, and volleyball. This program covers basic and more advanced techniques.  Summer Sports Experience is a drop-in program recommended for children ages 8-14. Occasionally a Summer Sports Experience program may be cancelled due to harsh weather or other conditions.Please note: We recommend that guardians accompany children participating in this program. items.title: Senior Cardio Sculpt
items.summary: This low impact cardio workout consists of functional movement exercises designed to make daily activities easier to perform.  Participants must be 60+ to attend this class. The site requires a separate form for the Department of Aging for all participants. Please come earlier to fill out the consent form.

items.title: Chair Yoga at Greeley Square Park
items.summary: Join the 34th Street Partnership at Greeley Square on Wednesday mornings for a rejuvenating, relaxing, and accessible chair yoga class. Our experienced instructors will lead you through a series of poses and stretches that will center your body and calm your mind.This class is perfect for people of all ability levels; no experience required. We recommend bringing a water bottle and wearing comfortable workout clothes.Registration for this event is recommended.

items.locationLabel: H.H. Biddle House (in Conference House Park)

items.title: Ongoing Museum Exhibit: Still Waters: Reflections of a Maritime Community

New Settlement Community Center requires all first-time participants to create a profile with the site upon arrival so please arrive at least 15 minutes in advance.

Whether you are a beginner or looking for a challenge- this class for you. Come engage in exercises that target all muscle groups and get your heart pumping!

items.title: intenSati
items.locationLabel: Myrtle Avenue and Park Lane South (in Forest Park)
items.venueAddress: Myrtle Avenue and Park Lane South (in Forest Park)
items.summary: In intenSati, we will prime your body, mind, and heart with this sweat-dripping, heart-pumping, mood-lifting cardio class (think dance meets kickboxing meets yoga). Class meets at Sgt. Schaefer Oval Lawn located at Myrtle Ave and Park Lane South.

items.title: Strong & Balanced Circuit Training
items.summary: This low-impact bodyweight circuit training class focuses on building strength, endurance, balance, and functional fitness through a variety of full-body exercises. Participants will improve overall conditioning while developing the core stability and balance needed for everyday activities and long-term health. All levels are welcome in this beginner-friendly class!Please bring a yoga mat and water.

items.title: Mat Pilates
items.locationLabel: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- Bedford-Stuyvesant Center
items.venueAddress: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- Bedford-Stuyvesant Center
items.summary: Mat Pilates is a beginner exercise class which concentrates on strengthening the body with an emphasis on core strength. The goals of this class are to improve posture, stabilize and elongate the spine, and to develop balance and overall strength. Mat Pilates is a great option for all fitness levels! Please bring your own mat.

items.title: Waterfront Workouts: Amp'd Bootcamp
items.locationLabel: Pier 2 (in Brooklyn Bridge Park),Brooklyn Bridge Park
items.venueAddress: Pier 2 (in Brooklyn Bridge Park),Brooklyn Bridge Park
items.summary: Push yourself with this free Amp’d Bootcamp class Brooklyn Bridge Park! This all-level one hour fitness class is open to all ages and abilities, led by instructors from Chelsea Piers Fitness. This is a part of Brooklyn Bridge Park's Waterfront Workouts series, offering free weekly workouts from May through September.Designed to diversify your workout, this bootcamp-style high intensity interval training (HIIT) class will incinerate calories and build strength. Come give your all at Brooklyn Bridge Park in this all-level cardio, strength, and plyometric-based workout, with a stunning waterfront view.No equipment is required but participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats or towels, if desired, to use on the turf.Advance registration is highly encouraged but walk-ups welcome as capacity allows. Fitness waivers are required by all participants. View all upcoming dates and full details at brooklynbridgepark.org. Please note holiday weekends are skipped and this event is subject to change due to weather or other extenuating circumstances.

items.title: Dance Fitness Beats
items.summary: This 45-minute Dance Fitness class is not just a great workout, but a great time as well! Come learn fun choreography to a vibrant mix of hip hop, reggaeton, soca, and Top 40 hits. If you're ready to let loose, sweat, and improve your cardiovascular health- join in!

items.title: Zumba
items.summary: Zumba is a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system! The routines feature aerobic, fitness interval training with a combination of fast and slow rhythms that tone and sculpt the body with easy to follow dance steps.

items.title: Salsa Social
items.summary: Join our friends from Mi Salsa Dura Baile for an evening of Latin rhythm and dancing in Garibaldi Plaza! Each class starts off with a free lesson followed by an open dance floor.

items.title: Circus Arts in Herald Square Park
items.summary: Try silk fan dancing, hoop tricks, contact juggling, plate spinning, and more! Our instructors can give you one-on-one guidance in a variety of flow and circus arts skills, or just drop by, pick up a prop, and have fun! All skill levels are welcome.

items.title: Caribbean Dance Fitness
items.locationLabel: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- East Harlem Neighborhood Health Action Center
items.venueAddress: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- East Harlem Neighborhood Health Action Center
items.summary: Caribbean Dance Fitness is a creative workout that fuses dance and aerobics. The goal is to improve cardio fitness while having fun and getting a full body workout! This class is taught to music with easy-to-follow steps that will surely get your heart pumping!

items.title: Dance Fitness Energize
items.summary: This 45-minute dance fitness class is about dancing your way toward an active lifestyle! Come and learn some fun and creative choreography for a full-body workout while enjoying a mix of upbeat music. All levels of fitness are welcome!

items.title: Body-Centric Circuit Training
items.summary: A low impact bodyweight workout, integrating holistic body empowering movements for improved overall strength and endurance. Align with your mindfulness to support inner strength and to connect with your body for a fulfilling fitness experience. All levels are welcome! Participants must sign in at the front desk and bring locks to lock up their bags. The center does not allow anyone to bring their bags to the dance room except towel, water and phone.

items.title: Tango in the Park at Sutton Place Park
items.summary: Tango in the Park at Sutton Place ParkStep into the rhythm of Buenos Aires right here in New York City! NYC Parks and Council Member Julie Menin invite you to experience the passion and elegance of Tango with Strictly Tango NYC Dance School. Whether you're a seasoned dancer or a complete beginner, this is your chance to learn from the best in an inviting, no-pressure environment.Wednesdays | 6:00 p.m. – 7:30 p.m.September 2, 9, 16, 23, and 30, 2026Sutton Place ParkE. For more information visit nyc.gov/parks or call (212)408-0243. Contact accessibility@parks.nyc.gov or (212) 360-1430 for more information regarding accessibility.

items.title: Summer on the Hudson: Yoga- Evening Salute to the Sun
items.locationLabel: The Plaza at 66th Street (in Riverside Park South)
items.venueAddress: The Plaza at 66th Street (in Riverside Park South)
items.summary: End your day with yoga in a beautiful sunset setting led by instructor Meg SantaMaria of Roadside Yogi. Suitable for all fitness levels. Please wear comfortable clothing and bring your own mat.

items.title: Zumba
items.summary: Zumba is a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system! The routines feature aerobic fitness interval training with a combination of fast and slow rhythms that challenge both the heart and muscles. With fun music and easy-to-follow steps, you can’t go wrong!

items.title: Movies Under the Stars: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl
items.locationLabel: Jackie Robinson Park -  Bandshell (in Jackie Robinson Park)
items.venueAddress: Jackie Robinson Park -  Bandshell (in Jackie Robinson Park)
items.summary: Grab a blanket and come enjoy a movie in a neighborhood park or playground! This summer, NYC Parks and The Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment will host family-friendly movie showings across the five boroughs.On an empty road in the middle of the night, Shula stumbles across the body of her uncle. As funeral proceedings begin around them, she and her cousins bring to light the buried secrets of their middle-class Zambian family.Rated PG-13 Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13. Parents are urged to be cautious.Movies begin at dusk. This event is FREE and open to the public. Glass bottles and alcoholic beverages are strictly prohibited. In the event of heavy rain or extreme weather, the screening may be canceled. The decision to cancel the event will be made prior to the screening and will be promptly posted on our website.For more information visit nyc.gov/parks or call 311. Contact (212) 360-1430 or accessibility@parks.nyc.gov for more information regarding accessibility.

items.title: Forest Fitness
items.locationLabel: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)
items.venueAddress: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)
items.summary: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. All classes end with closing with stretches.(Note: Fitness Walking does not meet if it is raining or if the actual temperature or wind chill is below 20 degrees F.)

items.title: Total Body Fitness
items.summary: This fun low-impact full-body workout includes cardio, strength and balance exercises to improve your overall fitness.

items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
items.summary: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

items.title: Trail Work Thursdays
items.locationLabel: VCPA Learning Garden (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.venueAddress: VCPA Learning Garden (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.summary: Be a part of the community effort to maintain the trails in Van Cortlandt Park. Whether you’re an experienced trailblazer or new to trail maintenance, your help will make a significant impact!Meeting Details:Location: VCPA Learning Garden - 6000 Mosholu Ave, Bronx, NY 10471. Across from the Riverdale Stables.Time: 9 am sharp; work begins at 9:15 am.Upcoming Activities Include:Clearing debris and overgrowthEnsuring trail safety and accessibilityDesire line closuresWhat to Bring:Comfortable, weather-appropriate clothingClosed-toed shoesWater and a snackWhy Join Us?Contribute to the vitality and safety of the trails you love! Engage with fellow community members, learn about trail maintenance, and enjoy the satisfaction of hands-on work in the great outdoors.Necessary tools and gloves will be provided!Want to bring a group? This event is limited to small groups of 5 or less. If you would like to bring more 6 or more people, please reach out to stewardship@vancortlandt.org to schedule a separate event.

items.title: Functional Yoga
items.summary: This yoga session is designed to help you better understand how the body works by focusing on improving balance, strength, and flexibility. Join this class and rediscover fun facts about each body part that makes up the whole of who you are. Experience isn't necessary, and all levels are welcome- join in with an open heart and open mind.

items.title: Public Gallery Tour
items.summary: Solo and group exhibitions at Glyndor Gallery explore the dynamic relationships between nature, culture, and site. When exhibitions are on view in the spring, summer, and fall, Gallery Greeters lead public exhibition tours on Thursdays and Saturdays at 2PM, certain dates excluded. Visitors can expect an in-depth look at artworks on view in Glyndor Gallery and in the Sunroom Project Space, showcasing the work of both emerging and established artists in the unique context of a public garden.  Each tour lasts approximately 45 minutes. Registration is not required for this drop-in event. Today’s tour features current exhibitions. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251.    Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with an elevator that provides access to the gallery level. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant.

items.title: Spotlight tour: Horticulture
items.summary: Dig deep into the High Line’s horticulture with a garden-focused tour! Each led by a knowledgeable High Line Docent, these 90-minute specialized tours offer an immersive look into the High Line’s rich and distinctive horticulture. Participants will gain a deep understanding of legendary garden designer Piet Oudolf’s naturalistic approach to plant selection, how the park’s over 500 species of plants contribute to the thriving ecosystems on the High Line and New York City, and much more.Horticulture tours will be led by docent Barbara Rohdie on September 3 and October 1.

items.title: City Council District 41: Monthly Gardener Gatherings
items.summary: All community gardeners and volunteers stewarding gardens in City Council District 41 are welcome to these monthly coalition-building events led by GreenThumb Community Engagement Coordinator, Hannah Wargo. Designed to increase collaboration and communication throughout the district’s 39 active community gardens—come meet fellow gardeners, share a meal, and discuss how we can further cultivate a thriving community garden district. Attendees can receive additional supplies and targeted support. Learn more, submit questions/topics suggestions, and RSVP here.Please save the following dates:Thursday, September 3rd:Location: Fred McLeod Community Garden, 1833 Strauss St. Rain or Shine!Topics: Summer Youth Employment Program, Sources of Support, Council Member FundingThursday, October 1st:Location: Phoenix Community Garden, 16 Somers St.Potential Topics: Project/Area Management, Collaborations, FinancesThursday, November 5th: Location and Topics To Be Determined

items.summary: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.One of the city's most iconic parks, Flushing Meadows Corona Park was the site of two 20th-century World's Fairs. items.title: Movies Under the Stars: Golden Door
items.locationLabel: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street (in Inwood Hill Park)
items.venueAddress: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street (in Inwood Hill Park)
items.summary: Grab a blanket and come enjoy a movie in a neighborhood park or playground! This summer, NYC Parks and The Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment will host family-friendly movie showings across the five boroughs.Imaginative and enthralling romantic drama about a rustic Sicilian widower (Vincenzo Amato) who gets involved with a mysterious, aristocratic Englishwoman (Charlotte Gainsbourg) on an immigrant ship en route to America in 1904. The film title refers to the metaphoric passage made by passengers through Ellis Island and into the New World. Written and directed by Emanuele Crialese. Also known as "Nuovomondo."Rated PG-13: Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13. Parents are urged to be cautious.Movies begin at dusk. This event is FREE and open to the public. Glass bottles and alcoholic beverages are strictly prohibited. In the event of heavy rain or extreme weather, the screening may be canceled. The decision to cancel the event will be made prior to the screening and will be promptly posted on our website.For more information visit nyc.gov/parks or call 311. Contact (212) 360-1430 or accessibility@parks.nyc.gov for more information regarding accessibility.

items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
items.summary: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

items.summary: Join the Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for forest restoration along the southern section of the Old Croton Aqueduct Trail. Dates are 10/2, 10/9, 10/16, 10/23, and 10/30.Meeting Details:Location: Classic Playground, Van Cortlandt Park South and Gouverneur Avenue. Meet at the public restroom building inside the playground.Time: 9:00 am - 12:00 pm.What to Bring:Long sleeves, long pants and sturdy closed-toed shoesWater and a snackTools, gloves and guidance provided; no experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Groups of 6 or more, please email noel@vancortlandt.org first.

items.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
items.summary: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

items.title: Proximity Exhibition
items.locationLabel: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.venueAddress: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.summary: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.

items.summary: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information.  Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side?  On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence.  You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. Friday, October 2, 2026 Saturday, October 3, 2026 Friday, October 9, 2026 Saturday, October 10, 2026 Friday, October 16, 2026 Saturday, October 17, 2026 Friday, October 23, 2026 Saturday, October 24, 2026 Friday, October 30, 2026 Saturday, October 31, 2026 - Halloween Special 9:00-10:30 PM Where: Visitor Services Booth, intersection at Chapel Road and Gazebo Road (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

items.title: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park
items.summary: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

items.title: NYRR Open Run: Inwood Hill Park
items.locationLabel: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street Entrance (in Inwood Hill Park)
items.venueAddress: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street Entrance (in Inwood Hill Park)
items.summary: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

items.title: It's My Park at Wolfe's Pond Park
items.summary: DIG+RIDE = FUN Join NYCMTB on the First Saturday of each month to help build, ride, and maintain the trails at Wolfe's Pond park in Staten Island. Volunteers help conduct our monthly trail inspection and perform routine maintenance tasks such as litter pickup, raking, erosion control (digging) and signage maintenance. Trail leaders will take teams into the network of trails. NOTICE: 1) Volunteers must arrive on time at 9:00 am. 2) Children 17 and under must be accompanied by an adult. 3) Volunteers must wear durable shoes: boots or sneakers. Volunteer groups may be walking up to a few miles. 4) Read about and protect yourself from ticks.﻿Optional group off-road mountain bike ride at 12:30pm on the trails (The route: mostly beginner friendly; distance: ~7 miles). Both groups meet at the Maintenance Shop in the Main Parking lot at Wolfe's Pond Park – 475 Cornelia Ave, Staten Island, NY 10312. Please register in advance: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/first-saturdays-wolfes-pond-park-tickets-1995158408508?aff=erelpanelorg

items.title: City of Forest Day
items.locationLabel: Greenbelt Nature Center (in Blood Root Valley)
items.venueAddress: Greenbelt Nature Center (in Blood Root Valley)
items.summary: Join us for the 5th annual City of Forest Day, when we will be planting climate adapted trees, shrubs, and herbaceous plugs to restore the understory near the Nature Center trail for years to come.  Presented by Forest for All NYC in partnership with the Parks and Open Space Partners coalition and NYC Department of Parks and Recreation (NYC Parks), City of Forest Day is an annual day of activities across the city to raise awareness of the importance of the New York City urban forest, and the essential role New Yorkers play every day in caring for the “lungs” of our city.Additional instructions:  Dress in long pants and sleeves and wear sturdy boots or sneakers suitable for standing on uneven terrain and digging in the soil.

items.title: BollyX
items.summary: BollyX is a Bollywood inspired cardio dance fitness class inspired and is driven by the heart-pumping, energetic rhythms of cultural music from all parts of India. The class embodies dynamic choreography and easy-to-follow dance aerobics. Choreography and workout routines have been set so everyone can enjoy the class (modifications for individual steps can be provided in class). No dance experience or Bollywood familiarity is required - just come with comfortable shoes, water, and your smiles!

items.title: City of Forest Day: Mini Rapid Site Assessment (RSA) at Forest Park
items.summary: Join NYC Parks Conservation and Monitoring team and learn about the rapid site assessment protocol as part of City of Forest Day. This process was designed as part of our forest management framework to quickly assess the ecological health of a specific forest area. Participants will learn about this process, how NYC Parks uses it, and how plant identification is a key component of this process. Please bring water and a snack as well as your smartphone or camera. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long socks, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty.  Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone.  To sign up a group of 2 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.

items.title: City of Forest Day: Brady's Pond Park Forest Restoration
items.summary: Volunteer with the NYC Parks Stewardship Team for City of Forest Day across New York City! Join NYC Parks in Brady's Pond Park as we celebrate our love of NYC’s urban forest and help steward the land. Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been made possible with funds from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.

items.venueAddress: Stephens Ave & O'Brien Ave (in Pugsley Creek Park)
items.summary: For City of Forest Day, join NYC Parks staff on a hike around Pugsley Creek Park to explore the diversity of fall fungi. Volunteers will learn how to identify these organisms and learn how to make iNaturalist observations of any other signs of nature you find along the way. Please bring water and a snack as well as your smartphone or camera! We will stay on trails and the hike will not be strenuous, but we will be walking for about an hour, so please dress appropriately. If you do not know how to use iNaturalist, arrive 15 minutes early and we will show you how! To sign up a group of 5 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.

items.title: Third United Lenape / Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow
items.locationLabel: Lefrak Center at Lakeside (in Prospect Park)
items.venueAddress: Lefrak Center at Lakeside (in Prospect Park)
items.summary: Join Prospect Park Alliance, the nonprofit that sustains Prospect Park in partnership with the city, Éenda-Lŭnaapeewáhkiing Collective, which brings together Lunáapeew/Lenape communities who have been displaced across Turtle Island (North America), and American Indian Community House, which promotes the well-being and visibility of the American Indian community, for the Third United Lenape/Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside in Prospect Park.Vendors will be open starting at 10 am and the Grand Entry will kick off the celebrations at 11 am each day.Please note that eventbrite RSVP is encouraged but not required.The first Pow Wow held in Prospect Park since 1972, and the third ever Lenape Pow Wow in New York City, this free, two-day public event welcomes the original Indigenous Lenape peoples who were forced to relocate across the continent back to their ancestral homelands to reunite and share their cultures with Brooklynites today. Join the weekend of family friendly fun, culture, art and learning with Indigenous dancers, drummers, and artisan craft and food vendors.Learn more about the Pow Wow here.The Pow Wow is part of the Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the Lefferts Historic House museum to explore the lives, resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family.To explore more Lenape heritage and culture, we encourage you to visit the Halumii Ktapihna: Lenape Legacies and Futures exhibit at the Museum of the City of New York, beginning September 25.

items.title: Nature Exploration: City of Forest Day
items.locationLabel: Audubon Center at the Boathouse (in Prospect Park)
items.venueAddress: Audubon Center at the Boathouse (in Prospect Park)
items.summary: Join Prospect Park Alliance for nature education activities to learn about and celebrate New York City’s urban forest!Leaf Art, 10 am–12 pm: Let’s have fun exploring the unique features of trees and their uniquely shaped leaves. Let your creativity flourish as you craft art inspired by nature.Nature Detective, 10 am–12 pm: What can you discover when you slow down and look closely? Borrow a sketchbook and observation guide, then record your discoveries and sketch what catches your eye, just like a naturalist in the field!Fall Leaf Discovery, 12–1 pm: Join us as we delve into the wonder of nature! Are you curious about why and when trees shed their leaves? Gain hands-on experience in citizen science as we explore the Prospect Park environment and witness how changing temperatures affect the trees. We will provide you with a guide to help you record your observations. This program leaves the Audubon Center promptly at 12 pm.

items.title: Prospect Park: City of Forest Day Tour
items.summary: This event is part of City of Forest Day, a citywide effort to raise awareness of our urban forest. Admission is free!Prospect Park is home to Brooklyn’s largest and oldest forest, an important hotspot of biodiversity with over 30,000 trees of 200+ species. On this guided walking tour with Prospect Park Alliance touring partner, Turnstile Tours, we will explore the history of the stewardship of this forest over the past 150 years, looking at some of the park’s oldest trees, exploring the management practices developed by park co-designer Frederick Law Olmsted, the work of the Alliance to restore these urban woodlands over the past 30 years, and contemporary challenges to forests due to climate change and invasive pests.   Prospect Park is a 585-acre park located in the center of Brooklyn. Most tours will begin at the Brooklyn Public Library Central Library, 10 Grand Army Plaza. Some special tours begin and end at different locations, so please take note of this when booking, and read your confirmation message carefully. Click here for Google Maps directions, view our neighborhood map, or view the official Prospect Park map.

items.summary: Join the Bronx River Alliance for a free community paddle at Shoelace Park! A total of 4 waves of participants will be able to go on-water every hour of the event (11am, 12pm, 1pm, 2pm), with a maximum of about 15 participants per wave.Staff and volunteers will be on-water to ensure safety, but please keep in mind that this is not a guided tour of the river.Minors must be accompanied by an adult. items.title: Woodland Community Volunteer Workday
items.summary: Join Wave Hill staff in the Herbert and Hyonja Abrons Woodland to celebrate City of Forest Day! Volunteers will learn about the importance of urban forests while lending a hand in managing invasive species. Gain first-hand knowledge of ecological practices and get your hands dirty while applying them alongside our staff experts. Tasks may include pulling invasive plants or clearing pathways. Please dress appropriately: long pants, layered clothing, and sturdy shoes are required. Gloves and tools provided.   This program is appropriate for adults and children under 18 accompanied by an adult. For community groups interested in volunteering please contact volunteer@wavehill.org. Registration required; free daily admission to all registered participants. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251.  The Community Woodland Workday will occur in a woodland or meadow setting with mixed-material pathways, varying elevations and possible off-pathway trip hazards. Activities require standing, bending down, and carrying items.

Haiti” —12:00 p.m.–12:25 p.m. and 2:45 p.m.–3:05 p.m.The Acorn Tree - Russia” — 1:00 p.m.–1:20 p.m. "The Flower Children - African” — 1:45 p.m.–2:05 p.m. and 3:30 p.m.–3:50 p.m."Catch It and Run - Native American” — 2:15 p.m.–2:35 p.m. Bike Powered Events: Pedal your way to a delicious smoothie or spiral artMusic by DJ I AmoreSchedule subject to change2026 GreenThumb Fresh Chef ContestAlmira Kennedy Coursey Amphitheater at Herbert Von King ParkTompkins Ave. and Van Buren St. Brooklyn, NY 1121612:30 p.m.–3:00 p.m.Come cheer on community members who will show off their cooking skills at the GreenThumb Harvest Fair! The eight chefs competing this year took part in a preliminary cook-off by creating a home cooked dish and were selected based on this dish from a vote on Instagram and Facebook. This contest challenges participants to replicate their most delicious and nutritious version of a surprise dish demonstrated by guest chef, Hisham "Ham" El-Waylly, a chef, recipe developer, and video creator based in New York City. After the demonstration, contestants will then have a limited time to prepare their interpretation of the dish, while Marlon Rice of Bedford Stuyvesant Restoration Corporation MC's the event and visitors cheer them on! The cook-off will conclude with a panel of judges, including Chef Ham, Chef Shorne of the restaurant Fat Fowl, and Gillian Graham, Chef / Partner at Hart's restaurant, who will crown the top three 2026 Fresh Chefs. Learn more about the Fresh Chef Contest from this year's guest chef, Hisham "Ham" El-Waylly, on Instagram! \ GreenThumb Harvest Fair CompetitionThe winners of the 2026 GreenThumb Harvest Fair Competition will be announced and the winning photo submissions of veggies, herbs, fruit, and flowers that GreenThumb community gardeners and home gardeners grew will be displayed at Herbert Von King Park.All community gardeners are encouraged to bring their harvest to the event and contribute to the community cornucopia table. We will have a special place to display them during the day.

items.title: Summer on the Hudson: Little Red Lighthouse Festival
items.locationLabel: Little Red Lighthouse (in Fort Washington Park)
items.venueAddress: Little Red Lighthouse (in Fort Washington Park)
items.summary: Celebrate Manhattan’s only remaining lighthouse with the Urban Park Rangers, readings of the eponymous children’s book, live music, local organizations, and activities for all ages! Featuring performances by Moosiki Kids, Leadlights Ensemble, General Mischief Dance Theatre, and a special presentation of Jessica Ann Carp's Little Red Lighthouse Musical. As the Little Red Lighthouse is more than 140 years old and in need of care, it has been determined that the Lighthouse will again be only be open for a limited number of tours during this year’s Festival, led by the NYC Park Rangers! As in years past, tours will be first come, first served, with tickets distributed on site at 12pm. To safely and comfortably accommodate visitors, we have reduced the total number of visitors we can accommodate, and tours are limited to the first 200 attendees. We highly recommend that visitors looking to tour the lighthouse earlier in the day arrive before noon.Tickets will be timed for a 40-minute windowTicketholders are asked to arrive on time for their scheduled tour.The Little Red Lighthouse is beloved by New Yorkers and visitors alike. Join us in our quest to ensure that the Little Red Lighthouse can safely receive visitors for years to come. Together we can keep the light shining!

items.title: Adorned by Nature: Wildcrafted Jewelry & Botanical Accessory Workshop with Journei Bimwala
items.summary: Join Journei Bimwala for this 1.5–2 hour hands-on creative workshop that invites participants to explore the beauty, versatility, and artistic potential of plants through wearable art. Using both fresh and dried botanical materials, participants will create 2–3 unique handmade accessories such as earrings, bracelets, rings, hair accessories, and other botanical adornments using natural plant fibers and wildcrafted materials. The workshop encourages participants to see plants beyond food and medicine by highlighting their role in fashion, self-expression, culture, and art.Throughout the session, participants will learn simple techniques for designing and assembling wearable pieces using leaves, flowers, vines, seeds, grasses, and other natural materials. The workshop is designed to foster creativity, imagination, and a deeper connection to the natural world while introducing participants to sustainable and plant-based crafting practices. Participants will also explore how adornment has historically been used across cultures as a form of identity, celebration, and artistic expression.The workshop will conclude with a celebratory mini photoshoot where participants will wear and showcase their handmade creations. These portraits will highlight the elegance and versatility of plant-based fashion while documenting each participant’s creativity and personal style. The goal of the workshop is to create a joyful and inspiring experience that blends nature, art, fashion, and community while showing the many ways plants can be transformed into beautiful wearable pieces.

items.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
items.locationLabel: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.venueAddress: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.summary: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

items.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
items.summary: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

items.title: Proximity Exhibition
items.locationLabel: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.venueAddress: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.summary: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.

items.title: Listening back to Parley
items.summary: Join us for a discussion with exhibiting artists Angel Nevarez & Valerie Tevere and legendary hip-hop artist La Roka (Rokafella). Presented in conjunction with the exhibition As far as the ear can hear, this program revisits the artists' collaboration on Parley, one of four works in the exhibition that explores sound across the landscapes of the Bronx, New Orleans, and the Sonoran Desert. Originally commissioned for the 2015 exhibition When You Cut Into the Present, the Future Leaks Out at the Old Bronx Borough Courthouse, Parley, performed by pioneering Bronx b-girl Rokafella (Ana Garcia) and MC Lady L (Lynn Saunders) draws on the sampling techniques and lyrical traditions of early hip-hop to reanimate questions of truth, justice, and hope. Using the musical framework of call and response to form a multilingual dialogue between two voices, Parley reflects Nevarez & Tevere's ongoing interest in framing sound and listening as a transformative practice that connects fragmented histories and collective memory to open new forms of relation. Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant. The Glyndor Terrace Garden is accessible via a bluestone path that begins south of the Glyndor House entrance and continues along its western perimeter towards an ADA-compliant ramp located at the Glyndor Terrace Garden’s north entrance.

items.title: Opening Reception: Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures by Billy Cleary
items.locationLabel: Van Cortlandt House Museum (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.venueAddress: Van Cortlandt House Museum (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.summary: Van Cortlandt Park in PicturesPhotography by Billy Cleary Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3, 2026 | 3:00–5:00 PMVan Cortlandt House Museum presents Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures, a photography exhibition by Riverdale photographer Billy Cleary celebrating the landscapes, wildlife, and changing seasons of Van Cortlandt Park.A Riverdale resident for more than three decades, Cleary has spent years photographing the places and scenes that define his surroundings. His images capture familiar views of Van Cortlandt Park throughout the year, from tree-lined paths and expansive fields to the park’s ponds, wildlife, and historic entrances. Together, the photographs offer a personal portrait of one of the Bronx’s most significant green spaces through the eyes of a longtime neighbor.Cleary’s interest in photography took on new importance during the pandemic, when he began sharing more of his work on social media. Messages from people who were largely confined to their homes and looked forward to seeing his photographs encouraged him to continue documenting and sharing the landscapes around him. His work has since appeared in group exhibitions with the Riverdale Art Association and in solo exhibitions at the Riverdale-Yonkers Society for Ethical Culture and An Beal Bocht Café.The public is invited to meet the photographer and view the exhibition during an opening reception on Saturday, October 3, from 3:00 to 5:00 PM at Van Cortlandt House Museum. Light refreshments will be served.Please note: The opening reception is for guests ages 21 and over. IDs will be checked at the door.Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures will remain on view through November 8, 2026.Accessibility: at this time, the historic house is accessed using one set of stairs. The exhibition opening reception will take place on the first floor.

items.summary: Join Prospect Park Alliance, the nonprofit that sustains Prospect Park in partnership with the city, Éenda-Lŭnaapeewáhkiing Collective, which brings together Lunáapeew/Lenape communities who have been displaced across Turtle Island (North America), and American Indian Community House, which promotes the well-being and visibility of the American Indian community, for the Third United Lenape/Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside in Prospect Park.Vendors will be open starting at 10 am and the Grand Entry will kick off the celebrations at 11 am each day.Please note that eventbrite RSVP is encouraged but not required.The first Pow Wow held in Prospect Park since 1972, and the third ever Lenape Pow Wow in New York City, this free, two-day public event welcomes the original Indigenous Lenape peoples who were forced to relocate across the continent back to their ancestral homelands to reunite and share their cultures with Brooklynites today. Join the weekend of family friendly fun, culture, art and learning with Indigenous dancers, drummers, and artisan craft and food vendors.Learn more about the Pow Wow here.The Pow Wow is part of the Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the Lefferts Historic House museum to explore the lives, resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family.To explore more Lenape heritage and culture, we encourage you to visit the Halumii Ktapihna: Lenape Legacies and Futures exhibit at the Museum of the City of New York, beginning September 25.

This free, two-day public event welcomes the original Indigenous Lenape peoples who were forced to relocate across the continent back to their ancestral homelands to unite together again to share their cultures with Brooklynites today. Pow Wows are gatherings where Lenape/Lunáapeew and neighboring Indigenous nations socialize and celebrate life. Prospect Park hosted formal Pow Wows from 1916 to 1972. Reviving this tradition in Prospect Park provides the Lenape/Lunáapeew an opportunity to celebrate their culture in their homelands and offers Brooklynites of all backgrounds the chance to enjoy the drumming, dancing, singing, art, crafts and foods of the original stewards of this land.

items.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
items.locationLabel: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.venueAddress: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.summary: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

items.title: Meet the Artists: Tarik Jeremiah Brown and Camille Cooper
items.summary: Join us for a Meet the Artist program with Van Lier Community Trust Fellows Tarik Jeremiah Brown and Camille Cooper. At 2PM, Brown will discuss his site-responsive installation, Hush Harbor, which transforms the Sunroom into a contemporary, antebellum hush harbor—a secret gathering place of refuge and worship for enslaved people--through sculpture, moving image, and sound. This project draws on themes of Black survival and faith, exploring ideas related to embodied belief and the relationship between spirit and land. At 3PM, Cooper will discuss his Sun Porch exhibition, SHOWPIECE, which takes up entomological study as a metaphor for the ways trans and gender-variant people are scrutinized and classified by society. Cooper transforms the Sun Porch into an insectarium full of sculptural bugs contextual to the grounds of Wave Hill, fabricated from the packaging of hormone replacement therapy and other trans ephemera. This afternoon program includes conversations with the exhibiting artists and the activation of works on display.  Meet the Artist is an ongoing series of conversations between exhibiting artists, the curatorial team, and sometimes invited guests at Wave Hill. As part of the Sunroom Project Space, this program is designed collaboratively with the artists and takes various forms. Meet the Artist offers visitors, the artist's community, and others an opportunity to gain insight into the artist's creative process and the themes present in their work. Registration encouraged but not required, online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251.

items.title: Third United Lenape / Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow
items.summary: Join Prospect Park Alliance, Éenda-Lŭnaapeewáhkiing Collective and American Indian Community House for the Third United Lenape / Lunaapeew Nations Pow Wow at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside in Prospect Park. This free, two-day public event welcomes the original Indigenous Lenape peoples who were forced to relocate across the continent back to their ancestral homelands to unite together again to share their cultures with Brooklynites today. Pow Wows are gatherings where Lenape/Lunáapeew and neighboring Indigenous nations socialize and celebrate life. Prospect Park hosted formal Pow Wows from 1916 to 1972. Reviving this tradition in Prospect Park provides the Lenape/Lunáapeew an opportunity to celebrate their culture in their homelands and offers Brooklynites of all backgrounds the chance to enjoy the drumming, dancing, singing, art, crafts and foods of the original stewards of this land.

items.title: Works in Public Opening: 145th Street
items.locationLabel: 145th and the Hudson River (in Riverside Park)
items.venueAddress: 145th and the Hudson River (in Riverside Park)
items.summary: The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation invite you to the opening of Works in Public in Riverside Park at 145th Street, celebrating sculptures by Lindsey Francis Jones and Clare Burson.Lindsey Francis Jones, City in Shapes, City in FishCity in Shapes, City in Fish invites viewers into the artist’s visual language through a cityscape of abstract shapes and color. Inspired by the craft and community of printmaking, the work incorporates images of six fish etched onto selected plexiglass, contributed by fellow printmakers and artists: Laurissa Widrick, Felix Bladbjerg, Kait Waldman, Stan Overstreet, Barbara Ganmen, and Scarlett Patino.Clare Burson, Unearthed.UNEARTHED is an installation of three steel forms inspired by the ancient Plain of Jars in Laos. It asks us to consider the inevitable and unexpected ways that history imposes itself on the present. When experienced with its accompanying soundscape, UNEARTHED also reminds us that our shared public spaces are nexus points for an infinite number of narratives that connect individuals and communities across time, those who lived here before us and those who will come after us.

items.title: Works in Public Opening: Riverside Park South
items.summary: The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation invite you to the opening of Works in Public in Riverside Park South, celebrating sculptures by Alicia Ehni and Robert Franca.About the Artists & ArtAlicia Ehni, Balancing A Peruvian shaman once told Ehni to carry a lemon in her purse, that it brings great harmony in life and in interactions with others. Two fractured pre-Columbian ceramics carry ancient coastal knowledge, opening possibilities to imagine a different future. Balancing reflects on the fragile relationships between people, nature, and the built environment.Robert Franca, The ChairsThe Chairs explores family as the foundation through which we understand ourselves and the world. Seen through a child’s perspective, the chairs embody imagination, openness, and freedom from conventional rules. Their human-like forms suggest movement and the ability to change. Ultimately, the chairs speak to the importance of finding balance — within ourselves, within families, and in navigating the challenges and uncertainties of an ever-changing world.

items.title: EPA Presentation: Impacts of Tire Pollution on the Bronx River
items.summary: Join the Bronx River Ecology Team for a special guest presentation from EPA Region 2 researchers. The researchers will be presenting their findings from their 2025 pollution study on the Bronx River which looked at 6PPD-quinone, a toxic chemical released by vehicle tires that can harm freshwater ecosystems.This presentation will take place virtually on Zoom and will last about 45 minutes followed by Q&A.

items.title: Garden Conflict Transformation Circle— A 2-Month Journey for Community Gardeners | Session #1
items.summary: Even the most harmonious garden groups experience conflict—it's as natural as weeds sprouting between the tomatoes. But what if those challenging moments could become opportunities for deeper connection and stronger communities? Join mediators Skye Roper-Moses and Michelle Jackson for an intimate, two-month learning cohort designed specifically for community gardeners who are ready to transform the way they navigate conflict.Session 1: Conflict Transformation CircleShare real-life challenges in a confidential, supportive space with fellow gardeners. Together, you’ll co-create solutions and learn practical skills you can take directly back to your garden.Session 2: Conflict Transformation Experiential LabDeepen your practice through hands-on exercises. Learn how to address tensions before they take root and gain confidence facilitating difficult conversations. Register Here NYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

items.title: Hatha Flow

items.summary: Immerse yourself in the wonders of the night sky every Tuesday on the High Line! The friendly team from the Amateur Astronomers Association—with whom we’ve been partnering since the park’s opening—will be there with high-powered telescopes, ready to reveal the secrets of the cosmos.No experience is necessary and telescopes will be provided between sunset and park closure.This High Line program is free and open to visitors of all ages. items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
items.summary: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

items.title: Wetland Wednesdays: Phragmites Control and Native Planting at Van Cortlandt Park
items.locationLabel: Van Cortlandt Golf House (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.venueAddress: Van Cortlandt Golf House (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.summary: Join the Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland restoration along Van Cortlandt Lake. We cut back invasive phragmites (common reed) that crowds out native wetland plants and, as plants arrive, plant native willows and shrubs at the restoration sites.Dates include Wednesdays weekly from October 7th - October 28th. Dates are 10/7, 10/14, 10/21, and 10/28.Meeting Details:Location: Van Cortlandt Golf House. Meet outside the VCPA offices next to the bathrooms.Time: 9:00 am - 12:00 pm.What to Bring:Long sleeves, long pants and boots (phragmites stems are sharp and the ground is wet)Water and a snackTools, gloves and training provided; no experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Groups of 6 or more, please email noel@vancortlandt.org first.

items.title: Team RIVER Volunteers
items.summary: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

items.title: Volunteer Workday: Howard Garden
items.summary: Join Howard Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for an engaging volunteer day to prepare the garden for new raised beds! Volunteers can get involved with weeding, dismantling old raised beds, and leveling soil. We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks.Join us for the whole project!Day 1 (Wed. Oct. 7) – Garden Site PrepDay 2 (Sat. Oct. 10) – New Bed BuildingDay 3 (Wed. Oct. 21) – Filling Beds & PlantingHoward Garden was founded in the late 1980's by community activists and artists who've made a lasting impact in the Brownsville community. These gardeners are still active to this day, and are excited to pass along the knowledge and skills gained through decades of environmental stewardship. This is a great opportunity for beginner and seasoned volunteers looking to join a growing garden!Register here!For information about group volunteering, please contact the GreenThumb Volunteer Program at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

items.title: Gardening with Ground Covers
items.summary: Have you ever wanted an alternative to woodchips or landscape fabric? If so, this is a workshop for you. Ground covers are an excellent way to protect exposed soils while also providing habitat and improving soil stability. In this workshop we will explore a variety of garden situations, plants and expand the definition of “ground covers.” Participants will learn how to select, establish and design with ground covers. No matter the size of your garden, ground covers are a great step towards building a sustainable and more resilient community garden.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

items.summary: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. All classes end with closing with stretches.(Note: Fitness Walking does not meet if it is raining or if the actual temperature or wind chill is below 20 degrees F.)

items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
items.summary: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

items.venueAddress: VCPA Learning Garden (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.summary: Be a part of the community effort to maintain the trails in Van Cortlandt Park. Across from the Riverdale Stables.Time: 9 am sharp; work begins at 9:15 am.Upcoming Activities Include:Clearing debris and overgrowthEnsuring trail safety and accessibilityDesire line closuresWhat to Bring:Comfortable, weather-appropriate clothingClosed-toed shoesWater and a snackWhy Join Us?Contribute to the vitality and safety of the trails you love! Engage with fellow community members, learn about trail maintenance, and enjoy the satisfaction of hands-on work in the great outdoors.Necessary tools and gloves will be provided!Want to bring a group? This event is limited to small groups of 5 or less. If you would like to bring more 6 or more people, please reach out to stewardship@vancortlandt.org to schedule a separate event.

items.summary: Help us plan and prepare for the 5th annual Community Banquet, a yearly grassroots tradition highlights the plants and people of the Bronx River. items.title: Public Gallery Tour
items.summary: Solo and group exhibitions at Glyndor Gallery explore the dynamic relationships between nature, culture, and site. When exhibitions are on view in the spring, summer, and fall, Gallery Greeters lead public exhibition tours on Thursdays and Saturdays at 2PM, certain dates excluded. Visitors can expect an in-depth look at artworks on view in Glyndor Gallery and in the Sunroom Project Space, showcasing the work of both emerging and established artists in the unique context of a public garden.  Each tour lasts approximately 45 minutes. Registration is not required for this drop-in event. Today’s tour features current exhibitions. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251.    Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with an elevator that provides access to the gallery level. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant.

Each exercise will help loosen up your muscles and joints, as well as help develop a great foundation for overall improved strength and range of motion. Whether you are just getting started or looking to get back to basics, this class is open to all! Class normally meets at the Astoria Park Pool Deck, and in the event of light rain class will be moved to Playground A under the Triboro Bridge.

items.title: NYRR Open Run: Flushing Meadows Corona Park

items.venueAddress: United Nations Ave South Entrance (in Flushing Meadows Corona Park)
items.summary: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.One of the city's most iconic parks, Flushing Meadows Corona Park was the site of two 20th-century World's Fairs. It features historic walks, scenic trails, sports venues, and facilities for activities including soccer, baseball, tennis, volleyball, cricket, and more, as well as a recreation center, an indoor pool, lakes, trails, and many cultural and civic institutions.

items.title: Movies Under the Stars: Shrek (2001)
items.summary: Grab a blanket and come enjoy a movie in a neighborhood park or playground! This summer, NYC Parks and The Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment will host family-friendly movie showings across the five boroughs.A green ogre living a life of solitude in a far away swamp, Shrek is suddenly invaded by a horde of fairy tale characters, such as the Big Bad Wolf and the Three Little Pigs, all refugees of their homes who have been shunned by the evil Lord Farquaad. Shrek decides to offer Lord Farquaad a deal; he will rescue the beautiful Princess Fiona , who is intended to be Farquaad's bride, in exchange for peace and quiet at his swamp.Rated PGParental Guidance Suggested. Some Material May Not Be Suitable For Children. A PG-rated motion picture should be investigated by parents before they let their younger children attend.Movies begin at dusk. This event is FREE and open to the public. Glass bottles and alcoholic beverages are strictly prohibited. In the event of heavy rain or extreme weather, the screening may be canceled. The decision to cancel the event will be made prior to the screening and will be promptly posted on our website.For more information visit nyc.gov/parks or call 311. Contact (212) 360-1430 or accessibility@parks.nyc.gov for more information regarding accessibility.
