items.title: Author Talk with David Rocco: Fireboats of the FDNY
items.locationLabel: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)
items.venueAddress: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)
items.summary: For the last century and a half, FDNY fireboats have played a vital role in protecting New York City’s waterfront. On Thursday, October 8, the Bayside Historical Society welcomes author and photographer David Rocco for an illustrated presentation exploring the history and evolution of these remarkable vessels.With more than 500 miles of shoreline, New York City has long relied on specialized fireboats to respond to fires along the waterfront and aboard ships. Using historic photographs and images, Rocco will trace their development from the early wooden-hull tugboats to the highly specialized vessels that serve the city today.Rocco has been involved in numerous historic preservation and cultural projects throughout the Hudson Valley and New York City. In 2023, he prepared the successful nomination that placed the retired FDNY fireboat John D. McKean on both the State and National Registers of Historic Places. He currently serves as Vice President of the Fireboat McKean Preservation Project.The presentation will be followed by a question-and-answer session and book signing.Admission is $10 for BHS members and $15 for non-members. Purchase tickets on the BHS website: https://www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/author-talk-with-david-rocco-fireboats-of-the-fdny.This event is part of Bayside Historical Society's Author Talk at the Castle Series.

items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery

items.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
items.summary: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

items.title: Proximity Exhibition
items.locationLabel: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.venueAddress: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.summary: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.

items.title: General Interest Meeting
items.summary: Join Farmer Yon, our volunteers, and GreenThumb Community Engagement Coordinators Gregory Anderson and Rain Abdalla for an evening of collective visioning. The Hattie Carthan Herban Farm has undergone 8 community powered volunteer clean up days, where we learned about the history of the garden and the herbs growing there. Now, we must find ways to connect with this history while determining what the future holds. We seek to answer questions like:What does becoming a member of this garden mean?What are the roles and responsibilities of a member? How does the garden serve us and the public?Come ready to sip on herbal tea, journal and share your ideas - BYOT (bring your own tea!) If you've volunteered before and would like to brew something from the garden, please reach out to Rain.Abdalla@parks.nyc.gov ahead of time.RSVP here (bit.ly/HerbanFarmFriday)

items.summary: The Urban Park Rangers celebrate the tradition of camping and we look forward to welcoming you. Join us for an unforgettable overnight camping adventure in Flushing Meadows Corona Park, home to the iconic Unisphere. items.title: 2026 Spooky Snug Harbor Tour
items.locationLabel: Visitor Information Booth (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.venueAddress: Visitor Information Booth (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.summary: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information.  Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side?  On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence.  You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. Friday, October 2, 2026 Saturday, October 3, 2026 Friday, October 9, 2026 Saturday, October 10, 2026 Friday, October 16, 2026 Saturday, October 17, 2026 Friday, October 23, 2026 Saturday, October 24, 2026 Friday, October 30, 2026 Saturday, October 31, 2026 - Halloween Special 9:00-10:30 PM Where: Visitor Services Booth, intersection at Chapel Road and Gazebo Road (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

items.title: NYRR Open Run: Inwood Hill Park
items.locationLabel: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street Entrance (in Inwood Hill Park)
items.venueAddress: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street Entrance (in Inwood Hill Park)
items.summary: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

items.summary: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Called the “Gateway to the Bronx River,” 205-acre Soundview Park is located where the Bronx River opens into the East River. This urban green space is filled with grassy baseball and soccer fields, a cricket pitch, basketball courts, a running track, walking/biking paths, picnic fields, and more! With its extensive views of the water, Soundview Park celebrates the beauty of both the Bronx and East Rivers. The back part of our Open Run course has beautiful views of the Bronx River waterfront for participants to enjoy!

items.title: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park Hispanic Heritage Month Celebration Run
items.summary: Celebrate Hispanic Heritage with Open Run! Wear your home country’s colors!  NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

items.title: Broadway Beautification
items.summary: Join the Fort Tryon Park Conservancy and NYC Parks for some cleaning in Fort Tryon Park! Help beautify the park along the Broadway Promenade. Meet at the Broadway Greeting Garden at the Arden Street/Broadway entrance. Wear long pants, sturdy shoes, and get ready to improve the park’s ecology by removing debris and helping site preparations.  Tools and gloves will be provided but please bring a filled water bottle.Groups of 5+ must RSVP by emailing info@FortTryonParkTrust.org 2 weeks in advance.Volunteers under age 18 must be accompanied by an adult.Beautification Days along the eastern expanse of the park take place on the 2nd & 4th Saturdays of each month from March to November. The Fort Tryon Park Conservancy supports these volunteer opportunities by underwriting tools, horticultural supplies, and NYC Parks staffing to oversee projects.

items.title: Volunteer Workday: Howard Garden
items.summary: Join Howard Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a hands-on volunteer day building new garden beds--no power tools needed! This is an exciting project to be a part of. We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks.Join us for the whole project!Day 1 (Wed. Oct. 7) – Garden Site PrepDay 2 (Sat. Oct. 10) – New Bed BuildingDay 3 (Wed. Oct. 21) – Filling Beds & PlantingHoward Garden was founded in the late 1980's by community activists and artists who've made a lasting impact in the Brownsville community. These gardeners are still active to this day, and are excited to pass along the knowledge and skills gained through decades of environmental stewardship. This is a great opportunity for beginner and seasoned volunteers looking to join a growing garden!Register here!In the event of inclement weather, we'll reschedule this event to Sunday, October 11th.For information about group volunteering, please contact the GreenThumb Volunteer Program at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov. This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

items.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
items.locationLabel: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.venueAddress: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.summary: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

items.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
items.summary: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

items.title: Proximity Exhibition
items.locationLabel: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.venueAddress: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)
items.summary: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.

items.title: "The Light That Shines Through the Universe": Lectures and Meditations - Monuments to War
items.summary: As part of the public programming for Tuan Andrew Nguyen’s High Line Plinth commission, The Light That Shines Through the Universe, the High Line presents a monthly lecture and guided meditation series at the Spur. Presented in partnership with the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, the series invites visitors to engage more deeply with themes central to Nguyen’s work. Each session features a lecture by a scholar, artist, or cultural leader, followed by a guided meditation led by an invited practitioner.The series is hosted by Tashi Chödrön, Himalayan Programs and Communities Ambassador at the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, who, in her two decades with the Rubin, has led meditation programs for over ten years and is the current host of the Rubin’s Mindfulness Meditation podcast. Through this combination of intellectual and contemplative practice, the series invites audiences to pause, reflect, and consider the artwork’s historical and philosophical themes through both thought and experience.Closing the series, Nico Rodriguez, deputy director of Monuments Lab, considers Nguyen’s work alongside contemporary artistic approaches to memorialization. The discussion explores how artists reimagine monuments to war by transforming sites of violence into spaces for remembrance, reflection, and collective healing.The lecture will be followed by a guided meditation by Steve Clorfeine, a meditation teacher from the Shambhala tradition with over 40 years of experience.Rain date: October 11, 2 – 3pm

And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information.  Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side?  On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence.  You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. Friday, October 2, 2026 Saturday, October 3, 2026 Friday, October 9, 2026 Saturday, October 10, 2026 Friday, October 16, 2026 Saturday, October 17, 2026 Friday, October 23, 2026 Saturday, October 24, 2026 Friday, October 30, 2026 Saturday, October 31, 2026 - Halloween Special 9:00-10:30 PM Where: Visitor Services Booth, intersection at Chapel Road and Gazebo Road (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

items.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
items.locationLabel: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.venueAddress: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
items.summary: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

items.summary: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

items.summary: Pelham Bay Park was once inhabited by small camps of coastal native people loosely referred to as the “Siwanoy” or “Southern People”. The Siwanoy traded along a route similar to the path of the Siwanoy trail. Hike with the Urban Park Rangers along this historic route and learn about the Siwanoy’s history and way of life.

items.title: CANCELED: Gentle Yoga

items.venueAddress: Beach 17 O'Donohue Park (in Rockaway Beach and Boardwalk)
items.summary: Bring your family and friends for a fun filled day at the Rockaway Fall Festival. There will be a pumpkin maze, pumpkin patch, Mechanical rides, light refreshments, giveaways, arts & crafts, games and music.

items.title: Pétanque in the Park
items.summary: Never heard of Pétanque? Our expert friends at NYC’s oldest running Pétanque club will teach you. This French lawn bowling game from the early 20th century is easy to learn, and we provide the boules. Just bring yourself!

items.title: Saunksquas, Sassafras, and Moccasins: Walking Tour with Oleana Whispering Dove
items.summary: Join Oleana Whispering Dove for a walking tour on the Wave Hill Grounds, highlighting the rich legacy of the region’s Indigenous Saunksquas and the profound impact of these women throughout history.  This tour reflects on historical imprint of known figures like Sojourner Truth, Maya Angelou, Condoleezza Rice,  Susan B. Anthony, Matilda Cage, Lucretia Mott, and Gloria Steinem with earlier unsung female leaders known as Saunk Squa’s; Mama Nuchwe, Dostou, Wastawancett, Lyssie, Annetie Pownock. These Native American women held the highest-ranking leadership roles in their communities and were honored by European settlers with titles like Her Royal Majesty, The King’s Queen, and Indian Princess—recognizing their powerful status and influence as they played a pivotal role in governing their regional tribes, leading land negotiations, and signing land treaties. Walks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. A limited amount of walking sticks are available to borrow. Pace varies from a slow walk to moderate walk throughout.

items.title: Bodyweight Circuit Training
items.summary: This circuit training class combines bodyweight resistance training and conditioning to provide you with a dynamic full body workout. Whether you are a beginner or looking for a challenge; this class for all fitness levels and modifications are always provided. Come engage in exercises that target all muscle groups, get your heart pumping, and connect with people in your community!

items.title: Zumba

items.title: BollyX
items.summary: BollyX is a Bollywood inspired cardio dance fitness class inspired and is driven by the heart-pumping, energetic rhythms of cultural music from all parts of India. Choreography and workout routines have been set so everyone can enjoy the class (modifications for individual steps can be provided in class). No dance experience or Bollywood familiarity is required - just come with comfortable shoes, water, and your smiles!Participants must sign in at the front desk and bring locks to lock up their bags. items.title: Forest Fitness
items.locationLabel: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)
items.venueAddress: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)
items.summary: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
items.summary: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

items.title: Hart Island Tour (North Island)
items.summary: Hart Island is the largest public cemetery in the country and has served New York City since 1869. While Hart Island is currently only used for city burials, the island is deeply connected to New York City institutions. It has served many uses since the 19th Century, including a military training ground, a quarantine station, a psychiatric hospital, a reform school, a rehabilitation facility, a missile base, and a jail.Join the Urban Park Rangers to explore Hart Island's unique past, present, and future. Participants are chosen by lottery. Lottery registration opens on Wednesday September 30, 2026 and ends Thursday October 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.  Please Note:-You must register each member of your party for the lottery under the same account. Anyone who was not registered will not be permitted to attend.-  If you are selected for the program, you will receive a series of emails confirming your selection and must respond as soon as possible to avoid forfeiting your spot. - Hart Island is only accessible via ferry. Selected participants will be provided details regarding program arrival and other specifics.- There are no indoor facilities, restrooms or drinking fountains on Hart Island. There are portable restrooms on the island.- This tour covers historical context of Hart Island and is about two hours of walking, some parts on uneven terrain. Please dress appropriately for the weather and the terrain.- Program may be cancelled due to inclement weather at the discretion of ferry operations.

Esta clase de Vinyasa Yoga incluye flujos de intensidad media que te llevarán desde el saludo al sol hasta una postura máxima final. Ven y concéntrate en las inversiones y la respiración para ayudarte a mejorar tu práctica personal mientras brindas conciencia y una nueva experiencia.  Se recomiendan tapetes, pero no son obligatorios, y todos los niveles son bienvenido. Connect, balance, and challenge yourself with Yoga in Spanish. This Vinyasa Yoga class includes mid-intensity flows that will move you seamlessly from sun salutation to a final peak pose. Come focus on inversions and breath work to help improve your personal practice while bringing awareness and a new experience. Mats are recommended but not required and all levels are welcome.

items.title: Cardio Dance
items.summary: This creative and fun workout fuses dance and aerobics to improve cardio fitness and tone the body.  Participants must sign in at the front desk and bring locks to lock up their bags. The center does not allow anyone to bring their bags to the dance room except: towel, water and phone.

items.title: Working with Rain: A Rain Garden Workshop
items.locationLabel: Escape to Nature (Glenmore Hendrix Block Association)
items.venueAddress: Escape to Nature (Glenmore Hendrix Block Association)
items.summary: This workshop aims to introduce attendees to the Rain Garden Stewardship Program, sponsored by the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEP). During the workshop, attendees will learn about the purpose and function of rain gardens, as well as the dos and don'ts of stewarding one. The public will also have the opportunity to sign up for the DEP program, which will provide all necessary equipment and materials for performing maintenance activities stewarding a rain garden.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

items.title: Dance Fitness
items.summary: Dance Fitness is a creative workout that fuses dance and aerobics. The goal is to improve cardio fitness while having fun and getting a full body workout! This class is taught to music with easy-to-follow steps that will surely get your heart pumping!

items.title: Bodyweight Circuit Training
items.summary: This circuit training class combines bodyweight resistance training and conditioning to provide you with a dynamic full-body workout. Whether you are a beginner or looking for a challenge- this class for you. Come engage in exercises that target all muscle groups and get your heart pumping! **Please bring a mat**

items.title: Hatha Flow
items.summary: The alignment-based hatha class invites you to slow down and reconnect with your breath and body through mindful movement. Together we’ll explore accessible postures, mobility, and body awareness in a supportive environment designed for all levels. Please bring a mat.  Participants must sign in at the front desk and bring locks to lock up their bags. The center does not allow anyone to bring their bags to the dance room except: towel, water and phone.

items.title: Yoga
items.summary: Connect with yourself in Yoga, a class to be enjoyed by all. Experience a fun and light-hearted, mid-intensity flow that will move you seamlessly from Sun Salutation to a final peak pose. We focus on inversions and breath work to ensure you leave class feeling challenged and balanced. Mats and recommended but not required.

items.title: Built To Move Circuit Training
items.summary: Built To Move is a full-body circuit training class that focuses on building strength and endurance while improving your mobility and stability. Whether you’re just getting started or a seasoned practitioner, we meet you where you are. No equipment, no limits. Just hard work and good vibes!Please bring a mat!

items.title: Dance Fitness World Wide Beats
items.summary: In this class, you will move to the music of Latin, Middle Eastern and Eastern European beats. Why? Because the combination of learning new movements and having fun is the best gift you can give to yourself! Everyone is welcome here.

items.title: Electro Dance Cardio
items.summary: Get ready to ignite your energy in this heart pumping dance cardio session! This class is designed to get the entire body moving at its full potential. Let loose and have fun as we move to electro-pop hits from all the decades.

items.title: Zumba
items.locationLabel: P.S. 361 Beacon - Woodside on the Move
items.venueAddress: P.S. 361 Beacon - Woodside on the Move
items.summary: Zumba is a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system! The routines feature aerobic, fitness interval training with a combination of fast and slow rhythms that tone and sculpt the body with easy to follow dance steps.

items.title: Tone Up Tuesday
items.summary: Tone up Tuesday is a 45-minute total-body class that blends cardio and strength training to help you feel strong — all while fitting into real life. This class can be done entirely with bodyweight (no equipment needed). Light weights, bands, or other equipment are optional for those who want an extra challenge. Modifications are always offered, making this class great for all fitness levels. We recommend that you bring a towel, water bottle, and yoga mat.

items.title: Uplifted Dance Fitness
items.locationLabel: Multi-Use Room - 2nd Fl (in Sorrentino Recreation Center)
items.venueAddress: Multi-Use Room - 2nd Fl (in Sorrentino Recreation Center)
items.summary: Uplift your spirit with this dance fitness class! Come and enjoy an array of upbeat music featuring gospel. This class is a fusion of motivation, inspiration, fitness, and fun. Move your body, relax your mind, enjoy the community, and lift your spirit!

items.title: Fun with Fitness Circuit Training
items.summary: A total body workout to strengthen, build, and have fun through body weight exercises. All fitness levels are welcome!

items.title: NYRR Open Run: Brooklyn Bridge Park Hispanic Heritage Month Celebration Run
items.summary: Celebrate Hispanic Heritage with Open Run! Wear your home country’s colors!  NYRR Open Run brings free, weekly community-led, approximately 3 mile runs to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.The Open Run route offers views of the Brooklyn Bridge on the way out, the Statue of Liberty on the way back, and the Lower Manhattan skyline the whole way. Fornino is a great spot to get drinks and pizza after the run.

items.title: Zumba
items.summary: Zumba is a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system! The routines feature aerobic, fitness interval training with a combination of fast and slow rhythms that tone and sculpt the body with easy to follow dance steps.

items.title: Stargazing on the High Line
items.locationLabel: On the High Line at 13th Street (in The High Line),under The Standard, at 13th St. (in The High Line)
items.venueAddress: On the High Line at 13th Street (in The High Line),under The Standard, at 13th St. (in The High Line)
items.summary: Immerse yourself in the wonders of the night sky every Tuesday on the High Line! The friendly team from the Amateur Astronomers Association—with whom we’ve been partnering since the park’s opening—will be there with high-powered telescopes, ready to reveal the secrets of the cosmos.No experience is necessary and telescopes will be provided between sunset and park closure.This High Line program is free and open to visitors of all ages. No RSVP is required. Stargazing on the High Line is subject to cancellation due to overcast conditions or inclement weather. If a stargazing session needs to be cancelled, we’ll add an alert to the High Line's webpage.

items.title: Cardio Sculpt
items.summary: This cardio workout consists of functional movement exercises designed to make daily activities easier to perform. Meets at the athletic courts.

items.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
items.summary: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova.  Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

items.title: Wetland Wednesdays: Phragmites Control and Native Planting at Van Cortlandt Park
items.locationLabel: Van Cortlandt Golf House (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.venueAddress: Van Cortlandt Golf House (in Van Cortlandt Park)
items.summary: Join the Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland restoration along Van Cortlandt Lake. We cut back invasive phragmites (common reed) that crowds out native wetland plants and, as plants arrive, plant native willows and shrubs at the restoration sites.Dates include Wednesdays weekly from October 7th - October 28th. Dates are 10/7, 10/14, 10/21, and 10/28.Meeting Details:Location: Van Cortlandt Golf House. Meet outside the VCPA offices next to the bathrooms.Time: 9:00 am - 12:00 pm.What to Bring:Long sleeves, long pants and boots (phragmites stems are sharp and the ground is wet)Water and a snackTools, gloves and training provided; no experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Groups of 6 or more, please email noel@vancortlandt.org first.

items.title: Team RIVER Volunteers
items.summary: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

items.title: Senior Cardio Sculpt
items.summary: This low impact cardio workout consists of functional movement exercises designed to make daily activities easier to perform.  Participants must be 60+ to attend this class. The site requires a separate form for the Department of Aging for all participants. Please come earlier to fill out the consent form.

items.title: Chair Yoga at Greeley Square Park
items.summary: Join the 34th Street Partnership at Greeley Square on Wednesday mornings for a rejuvenating, relaxing, and accessible chair yoga class. Our experienced instructors will lead you through a series of poses and stretches that will center your body and calm your mind.This class is perfect for people of all ability levels; no experience required. We recommend bringing a water bottle and wearing comfortable workout clothes.Registration for this event is recommended.

items.title: Ongoing Outdoor Museum Exhibit: Alice's Terracotta Garden
items.locationLabel: H.H. Biddle House (in Conference House Park)
items.venueAddress: H.H. Biddle House (in Conference House Park)
items.summary: Terra cotta sculpture garden featuring antique architectural ornaments from Tottenville's Atlantic Terra Cotta Company (west side lawn of Biddle House).NYC Parks and the Tottenville Historical Society invite you to visit a unique collection of terracotta artifacts that chronicle turn-of-the-twentieth-century architectural styles common in New York City and across the United States.

items.title: Ongoing Museum Exhibit: New York's Brick & Terra Cotta Industries
items.locationLabel: H.H. Biddle House (in Conference House Park)

Brown & Sons Shipyard of Tottenville and spotlighting our recreational waterfront and more. Note location:  Rutan-Becket House, 6 Shore Rd. Open by chance or by appointment.

items.title: Step Aerobics
items.summary: Step Aerobics is a cardio workout that will elevate your heart rate, strengthen muscles, and improve coordination and balance.  Please register for updates about cancellations. Class is first come, first served, but for safety reasons, participants will not be allowed to join after the first fifteen minutes of class. New Settlement Community Center requires all first-time participants to create a profile with the site upon arrival so please arrive at least 15 minutes in advance.

items.title: Pétanque in the Park
items.summary: Never heard of Pétanque? Our expert friends at NYC’s oldest running Pétanque club will teach you. This French lawn bowling game from the early 20th century is easy to learn, and we provide the boules. Just bring yourself!

Please note: We recommend that guardians accompany children participating in this program. Kids in Motion is not a childcare program and NYC Parks is not responsible for the well-being of attendees.

items.title: Arts, Culture & Fun: BE BOLD: Ballet Programming
items.summary: NYC Parks, in partnership with the Misty Copeland Foundation, invites childrenages 6 – 14 years to enroll in the BE BOLD afterschool dance program, a funintroductory ballet class with live music. The BE BOLD program is FREE andoffers a new approach to afterschool dance education for young children that makes ballet accessible, affordable, and fun. *Membership required*Please email sarah.bishow@parks.nyc.gov to register.

items.title: Bodyweight Circuit Training
items.locationLabel: Rock Climbing Wall Room (in Gertrude Ederle Recreation Center)
items.venueAddress: Rock Climbing Wall Room (in Gertrude Ederle Recreation Center)
items.summary: This circuit training class combines bodyweight resistance training and conditioning to provide you with a dynamic full-body workout. Whether you are a beginner or looking for a challenge- this class for you. Come engage in exercises that target all muscle groups and get your heart pumping!

items.title: intenSati
items.locationLabel: Myrtle Avenue and Park Lane South (in Forest Park)
items.venueAddress: Myrtle Avenue and Park Lane South (in Forest Park)
items.summary: In intenSati, we will prime your body, mind, and heart with this sweat-dripping, heart-pumping, mood-lifting cardio class (think dance meets kickboxing meets yoga). Class meets at Sgt. Schaefer Oval Lawn located at Myrtle Ave and Park Lane South.

items.title: Mat Pilates
items.locationLabel: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- Bedford-Stuyvesant Center
items.venueAddress: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- Bedford-Stuyvesant Center
items.summary: Mat Pilates is a beginner exercise class which concentrates on strengthening the body with an emphasis on core strength. The goals of this class are to improve posture, stabilize and elongate the spine, and to develop balance and overall strength. Mat Pilates is a great option for all fitness levels! Please bring your own mat.

items.title: Strong & Balanced Circuit Training
items.summary: This low-impact bodyweight circuit training class focuses on building strength, endurance, balance, and functional fitness through a variety of full-body exercises. Participants will improve overall conditioning while developing the core stability and balance needed for everyday activities and long-term health. All levels are welcome in this beginner-friendly class!Please bring a yoga mat and water.

items.title: Zumba
items.summary: Zumba is a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system! The routines feature aerobic, fitness interval training with a combination of fast and slow rhythms that tone and sculpt the body with easy to follow dance steps.

items.title: Dance Fitness Beats
items.summary: This 45-minute Dance Fitness class is not just a great workout, but a great time as well! Come learn fun choreography to a vibrant mix of hip hop, reggaeton, soca, and Top 40 hits. If you're ready to let loose, sweat, and improve your cardiovascular health- join in!

items.title: Salsa Social
items.summary: Join our friends from Mi Salsa Dura Baile for an evening of Latin rhythm and dancing in Garibaldi Plaza! Each class starts off with a free lesson followed by an open dance floor.

items.title: Dance Fitness Energize
items.summary: This 45-minute dance fitness class is about dancing your way toward an active lifestyle! Come and learn some fun and creative choreography for a full-body workout while enjoying a mix of upbeat music. All levels of fitness are welcome!

items.title: Caribbean Dance Fitness
items.locationLabel: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- East Harlem Neighborhood Health Action Center
items.venueAddress: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene- East Harlem Neighborhood Health Action Center
items.summary: Caribbean Dance Fitness is a creative workout that fuses dance and aerobics. The goal is to improve cardio fitness while having fun and getting a full body workout! This class is taught to music with easy-to-follow steps that will surely get your heart pumping!

items.title: Body-Centric Circuit Training
items.summary: A low impact bodyweight workout, integrating holistic body empowering movements for improved overall strength and endurance. Align with your mindfulness to support inner strength and to connect with your body for a fulfilling fitness experience. All levels are welcome! Participants must sign in at the front desk and bring locks to lock up their bags. The center does not allow anyone to bring their bags to the dance room except towel, water and phone.

items.title: Brazilian Movement with Maria Assis
items.summary: Come join us to dance on the High Line! Brazilian movement is a unique and fun combination of Samba reggae from Bahia, Rio de Janeiro, and West African and Latino beats. All levels are welcome.This event is free and open to the public. All levels are welcome. Please wear comfortable clothes and shoes to move around in. Water will be provided.Advance registration is encouraged. Walk-ups are welcome. The event is rain or shine—the event space is fully covered. In the event of extreme weather, this program may be canceled for the health and safety of our visitors and staff. If a cancellation is necessary, Eventbrite registrants will be notified via email and we will post an update on our website.

items.title: Zumba
items.summary: Zumba is a fusion of Latin, International and popular music dance themes creating a dynamic, exciting, effective fitness system! The routines feature aerobic fitness interval training with a combination of fast and slow rhythms that challenge both the heart and muscles. With fun music and easy-to-follow steps, you can’t go wrong!

items.title: Latin Dance Fitness
items.summary: Come join us as we dance to a mix of salsa, bachata, merengue, 80’s and 90’s music.  All are welcome!    Please arrive 15 minutes early to complete a ONE-TIME Beacon Membership Form before you attend your first class.   Ven a unirte a nosotros mientras bailamos una mezcla de salsa, bachata, merengue, música de los años 80 y 90. Todos son bienvenidos  Por favor llegue 15 minutos antes para completar un Formulario de Membresía Beacon ÚNICO antes de asistir a su primera clase.
